body:
This isn't exclusive to the Game view, either. The 2D and 3D workspace toolbars also freely mix short action names and longer descriptions. When an action has a shortcut with a hotkey, usually the shorter name is used.

We should probably standardize a little more on short names (with optional longer descriptions underneath), because its more compatible with editor shortcuts. It's also a little friendlier to documentation; for example see https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/introduction_to_3d.html#main-toolbar, which lists all the toolbar buttons. The ones with long descriptions are a bit jarring.

Tested on:  v4.4.1

In addition, regarding shortcut hints, the Select Mode tooltip shows a bunch of shortcuts in Scene view:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bea3364-7746-453b-8397-6aa26c24dda7)

in particular:

> Alt+RMB: Show list of all nodes at position clicked, including locked. (Available in all modes.)

while the equivalent tooltip in the Embedded Game view says:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c0e7ab0-eac2-4717-af2f-84f25839395f)

> Ctrl+Alt+RMB: Show list of all nodes at position clicked.

(and Command+Alt on macOS, looking at OP)

I tested both on a Linux desktop where Alt+RMB shows a window contextual menu:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99647124-a444-46c9-9d4c-d60725191a44)

so I had to use add an extra modifier (Ctrl+Alt, Shift+Alt, or event Super+Alt as in the drag cancelling [Super+Alt trick](https://askubuntu.com/a/883073/334099) but that one was meant for LMB click).

So, I have a feeling that Alt+RMB *is* the minimum shortcut needed, and that the description in Scene view toolbar is the correct one. Now indicating Ctrl+Alt+RMB is useful for some Linux users, but may be misleading as it's not the Ctrl+Alt that does the job, but rather Alt, plus another modifier to cancel the window management contextual menu on some desktops.

Not sure what is best, assuming Linux users will now all the tricks (Alt+RMB) or giving them all the hints (Ctrl+Alt+RMB), either way the tooltips should be consistent.

What about macOS? Does Alt+RMB just work? In which case the Command+Alt+RMB tooltip is just plainly wrong.
